title: Working memory, Awareness of Choice (AoC) and Awareness of Action (AoA) in the decision-making process in a professional frame
abstract: Working memory significantly influences decision-making effectiveness and decisionmaking awareness encompasses Awareness of Choice (AoC) and Awareness of Action (AoA). Additionally, internal (i.e., personality traits, expertise) and external factors (i.e., time pressure, incentives) influence the quality of decision-making. This study investigated behavioural correlates of two professionals’ groups performing a novel dual task to explore AoC and AoA accuracy (ACC). 117 healthy individuals, divided into next-generation (N=75) and experienced professionals (N=42), completed the task, followed by the 10-item Big Five Inventory and Maximisation Scale. Findings indicate that experienced professionals have lower ACC than next-generation and that AoC turns out to be more difficult and cognitively demanding compared to AoA, maybe because thought processes are abstract and difficult to monitor and control. The lower awareness in experienced professionals, instead, could be attributed to work experience and work environment itself, that required to make complex, intuitive, and rapid decisions. Moreover, personality traits correlate differently with ACC in next-generation and experienced professionals, highlighting different personality patterns.
